gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, in tests by named reviewers, the VIOFO A229 Ultra's front camera recorded about 36 Mb/s with the 4K rear connected, against 59.87 Mb/s on its own. In the same kind of test, the Vantrue S1 Pro Max recorded 23.8 Mb/s on each of its two 4K cameras, and 31.9 Mb/s on the front after a late-2025 firmware update. So 'dual 4K' does not mean the same amount of picture detail per second on each camera.
standout_why: I read Product Bible's 'Best 4K Dash Cams of 2026' (cited, updated 2026-11-19). It lists the A229 Ultra and BlackVue Elite 10 2CH as dual 4K but gives no bitrate, no power draw and no measured heat. Its per-minute storage figures are maker ratings or the author's own arithmetic. VIOFO's own 4K collection page and FAQ (both cited) are maker pages, and VIOFO's A229 Ultra page does not say the front bitrate drops when the rear camera is added. I could not open Car and Driver's best-dash-cams list (the site blocked the fetch) or The Car Gear Guide (certificate error), so I cannot rule out those two. Vortex Radar's best-dashcams page also returned 403. Vortex Radar measured the 2CH drop, but in a DashCamTalk forum post, and none of the results ChatGPT got is that post. ChatGPT's answer listed the A229 Ultra as 'True 4K + 4K' and did not mention the Vantrue S1 Pro Max at all.
decides: This supports the A229 Ultra 2CH as the pick on recording quality. Even with the measured 2CH drop, its front plus rear comes to about 71 Mb/s (36.11 + 35). The S1 Pro Max comes to about 47.6 Mb/s on its June 2025 firmware, or about 55.7 Mb/s with the front raised to 31.9 Mb/s. The finding also corrects the impression that the Ultra's front records at 60 Mb/s in two-channel use. That holds on its own only, and VIOFO's newest front firmware (V1.2_260813) changelog does not say the 2CH bitrate was restored. The Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K honestly wins the lower-price dual-4K segment. The partner read gives it at $239.99 pay-today on 2026-11-21, against $409.99 for the A229 Ultra 2CH at viofo.com on 2026-11-21. Both cameras use Sony IMX678 sensors front and rear and have supercapacitors. The trade-off is a lower recorded bitrate and a warm rear module, so Vantrue places in the top three on the question's own terms.

findings.label: Front-camera bitrate, front + 4K rear recording together (2CH)
findings.source_title: Viofo A229 Ultra vs. A229 Pro & A329S (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Measured by Vortex Radar, posts #12 and #16, Aug 19-20, 2025. He measured 59.87 Mb/s in 1CH (front only) and 36.11 Mb/s in both 2CH and 3CH. He wrote that 'the bitrate on the A229 Ultra's front cam also drops as you add more channels' and that his earlier short 10-20 s clips had given a different figure. rcg530 (post #13, Aug 19, 2025, front fw 1.0_250804, rear 4K_V1.0_250620) could not reach the 40.94 Mb/s figure from an earlier version of that post in 2CH.

findings.label: Rear-camera bitrate and 1-minute file size (4K rear)
findings.source_title: A229 Ultra Test & Review PP (DashCamTalk forum, Chuck McCoy)
findings.note: Chuck McCoy, post #1, Aug 10, 2025, gave 35 Mbps / 250 MB for the rear and the waterproof rear, alongside a maximum of '60 Mbps / 430MB Front' in 2CH and 36 Mbps / 260 MB in 3CH. His post #3 (Aug 17, 2025) measured the RWE800 waterproof rear at 35 Mbps and 255 MB per minute (fw 4KW_V1.0_250620). In post #17 of the comparison thread (Aug 20, 2025) he wrote that 'the next firmware update should restore 60Mbps to the front camera in 2CH rear configuration.'

findings.label: Current firmware and changelog
findings.value: Front V1.2_260813 (released 2026-08-13), changelog 'Fixed: Other bugs'; rear V1.1_260126, changelog 'Fixed some bugs'
findings.note: Neither A229 Ultra entry mentions bitrate. Whether the 2CH front bitrate went back to 60 Mb/s is not stated by VIOFO.

findings.label: Channels, sensors, card, US store price
findings.value: 2-channel (front + rear window), both 3840×2160, both Sony STARVIS 2 IMX678 with HDR; microSD up to 512 GB; quad-mode GPS; $409.99
findings.source_title: VIOFO A229 Ultra 2CH 4K Front+4K Rear Dashcam with Dual Sony STARVIS 2 Sensors
findings.note: Read from the VIOFO Shopify store data, listed as available. No compare-at price. The HK4 hardwire kit is $17.99 at viofo.com on the same date.

findings.label: Bitrate, front + rear recording together
findings.value: 23.8 Mb/s each camera; front raised to 31.9 Mb/s by the late-2025 firmware
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue S1 Pro Max (DashCamTalk forum, EricSan)
findings.note: EricSan, first post, Jun 22, 2025: front + rear 'each at 23.8Mb/s'. A later undated edit to that post says the end-of-2025 update raised the front to 31.9 Mb/s, a 33% increase. TonyM's thread (https://dashcamtalk.com/forum/threads/review-4k-4k-vantrue-s1-pro-max.53493/, post #17, Jul 22, 2025, fw VT-EEF243) measured 24.6 Mb/s front and 23.8 Mb/s rear on a daytime highway drive (H.265, PlatePix on, HDR off).

findings.label: Power draw
findings.value: About 8.7 W driving with both cameras, screen and Wi-Fi on; about 4.1-4.2 W in low-bitrate parking (1080p 15 fps, screen off)
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue S1 Pro Max (DashCamTalk forum, EricSan)
findings.note: EricSan, posts #15 and #19, Jun 22-23, 2025. Front with GPS alone measured 4.9 W. He notes the manual lists 6 W. The hardwire kit gave 5.05-5.08 V with both cameras running.

findings.label: Rear camera surface temperature
findings.value: 54 °C on the back panel at 22 °C room ambient (32 °C rise)
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue S1 Pro Max (DashCamTalk forum, EricSan)
findings.note: EricSan, post #5, Jun 22, 2025, recorded indoors. Dash Cam Guys repeats the reading for the RC11 rear camera.

findings.label: Storage used with both channels at 4K
findings.value: About 21 GB per hour, about 47 hours on a 1 TB card (Vantrue's listing claims up to 86 hours)
findings.source_title: Vantrue S1 Pro Max Review: Dual 4K, and What It Gives Up (Dash Cam Guys)
findings.note: Dash Cam Guys credits this to DashCamTalk independent testing, with no tester name or date. The figure agrees with 2 × 23.8 Mb/s = 47.6 Mb/s ≈ 21.4 GB/h. The same review says the camera uses a supercapacitor, has a 155° front and rear field of view, has no 60 fps mode, and that all four parking modes need constant power (it recommends Vantrue's VP05 hardwire kit).

findings.label: Arithmetic comparison of combined recorded bitrate
findings.value: A229 Ultra 2CH ≈ 71 Mb/s (36.11 + 35) vs S1 Pro Max ≈ 47.6 Mb/s (Jun 2025 fw) or ≈ 55.7 Mb/s (31.9 + 23.8 after the late-2025 fw)
findings.source_title: Viofo A229 Ultra vs. A229 Pro & A329S (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: My sum of the figures above. The two cameras were measured by different testers on different firmware, so treat this as a guide, not a lab comparison. At about 71 Mb/s, the A229 Ultra 2CH uses about 32 GB per hour, roughly 16 hours on its maximum 512 GB card (my arithmetic).

unsourced: Whether VIOFO's current A229 Ultra front firmware (V1.2_260813) brings the 2CH front bitrate back to 60 Mb/s. The changelog says only 'Fixed: Other bugs', and I found no post-update measurement.
A measured power draw or parking-mode draw for the A229 Ultra. A search found only A229 Pro and Plus figures, which are not used here.

Measured bitrate, power or temperature for the BlackVue Elite 10 2CH, 70mai A900 Ultra and Rexing R88. I did not find these within the tool budget, and I did not verify that the 70mai and Rexing models record 4K on the rear.

A measured night plate-reading distance for any dual-4K candidate. Dash Cam Guys states it has published no controlled plate-reading measurement for the A229 Ultra, and TonyM's S1 Pro Max thread describes plates only in words.

Vantrue's own S1 Pro Max 4K+4K product page: vantrue.com returned HTTP 429 three times, so I could not confirm the maker's GPS, rated bitrate or bundled hardwire kit, or read today's price myself. The $239.99 figure comes from the partner read supplied in the brief.

Car and Driver's best-dash-cams list (cited by ChatGPT) and Vortex Radar's best-dashcams page could not be opened (fetch blocked or 403), so I could not check whether either states the 2CH bitrate drop.
